title: Ensemble Methods
subtitle: Bagging, boosting, Random Forest, and XGBoost

content.text: Ensembles combine multiple models to outperform any single model. The two main strategies are bagging (parallel, reduces variance) and boosting (sequential, reduces bias).

content.code:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier, GradientBoostingClassifier

# Random Forest (bagging)
rf = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, max_depth=None, random_state=42)
rf.fit(X_train, y_train)

# XGBoost (gradient boosting)
from xgboost import XGBClassifier
xgb = XGBClassifier(n_estimators=200, learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=6)
xgb.fit(X_train, y_train, eval_set=[(X_test, y_test)], early_stopping_rounds=10)

print("RF score:", rf.score(X_test, y_test))
print("XGB score:", xgb.score(X_test, y_test))

content.text: XGBoost and LightGBM win most structured-data Kaggle competitions. Use them as a strong baseline.

questions.question: What does Random Forest use to create diversity among trees?
options: Random subsets of data and features
questions.explanation: Random Forest samples both rows and features randomly for each tree, creating diverse trees that together are more accurate.

faq.q: When should I use boosting vs bagging?
faq.a: Bagging (Random Forest) works well out of the box and is hard to overfit. Boosting (XGBoost) is more accurate but needs careful tuning of learning_rate and n_estimators.
